hook.text: Cutting raw chicken then slicing tomatoes on the same board—that's how most home food poisoning happens.

buildup.text: Cross-contamination transfers pathogens from raw to ready-to-eat food through surfaces, hands, utensils, or splash.

discovery.text: Color-coded cutting boards prevent it: red for raw meat, green for vegetables, blue for fish—visual separation systems.

twist.text: Reusable grocery bags tested positive for E. coli in 8% of samples. Last week's chicken bag contaminates today's salad.

climax.text: In commercial kitchens, the flow of food is designed so raw and cooked never cross paths—separate sinks, separate zones.

punchline.text: Raw and ready-to-eat should never touch. Separation prevents sickness.

quiz.question: Why do commercial kitchens use color-coded cutting boards?
options: To visually separate raw and ready-to-eat food preparation areas
